newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 18.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 18.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
HAMBURG - Advertising agency Baader, Lang, Behnken plans a
management and ownership reshuffle, says its owner, ad group AP
Lintas. Retreating from statements they made in April that they
wanted to buy the agency back from AP, joint chief executives
Fred Baader and Wolfgang Behnken now plan to leave the company
by the end of the year and sell their shares, AP Lintas says.
(Reuter)
WALLDORF - French tourist office Maison de la France gives its
entire advertising account to McCann-Erickson Frankfurt. The
agency won out over Bozell and former account holder Publicis
Frankfurt. (Kress)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
MUNICH - The president of the Federal Cartel Office, Dieter
Wolf, renews criticism of the pay-TV deal between media groups
Bertelsmann and Kirch, after meetings with both companies. Wolf
tells the Sueddeutsche Zeitung that several concerns could stop
the alliance. (Reuter)
BONN - German publishing houses in 1996 used about five million
tons of paper for newspapers, magazines and catalogues, causing
publishing associations and paper manufacturers in Bonn to sign
an agreement to use more environmentally friendly production
methods. (Die Welt)
BERLIN - Publishing house Axel Springer Verlag AG posts first
half net profits of over 100 million marks ($55.8 million),
compared to 80.5 million in the same period a year earlier.
Group operating profit reaches 229 million marks, up from 156
million marks. (Reuter)
MAINZ - Both public broadcaster ZDF and private channel RTL
announce they plan to broadcast the "traditional summer
interview" with Chancellor Helmut Kohl. ZDF says it will
broadcast the interview on August 17, while RTL plans to show it
during the first week in August. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
VEVEY, Switzerland - Swiss food and beverage conglomerate
Nestle SA says the growth rate for group sales will likely ease
in the second half of the year compared with the first half due
to the expected development of foreign exchange rates. Nestle
also says it is confident the internal growth rate will continue
in the second half of 1997. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Two rumoured suitors for Karstadt AG, whose shares
have surged more than 100 marks this week on takeover
speculation, deny interest in taking a stake in the German
retailer. German holding group WCM AG and Dutch supermarket
group Ahold NV both say they are not interested in the retailer.
(Reuter)
MUNICH - Siemens AG is headed for a clear pretax profit rise
this year even though the company itself has forecast no
improvement, two German business magazine report. Manager
Magazin, attributing company plans, says pretax profit is seen
rising to over four billion marks, thanks to a 300 million mark
improvement in medical technology results, firmer semiconductor
prices and a smaller than expected loss in the transportation
technology unit. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - German's Ifo economic research institute says its
business climate index for west Germany rose beyond market
expectations in June to 96.0 from a revised 95.4 in May. In east
Germany the business climate reading eased back slightly with
the index at 103.6 from an upward revised 103.7 in May, Ifo
says. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Carmakers Volkswagen AG and Ford-Werke AG say they
are launching a recall action that will affect about 20,000
minivans produced as part of their joint venture in Portugal. VW
and Ford-Werke, the German unit of U.S. carmaker Ford Motor Co,
say the recall for vehicles sold throughout Europe is needed to
replace a part in the five-point-seatbelt for a child's seat.
(Reuter)
BREMEN - The German unit of struggling South Korean car maker
Kia Motors Corp says German and European business are not being
hurt by the parent company's financial turmoil. So far this year
Kia has exported 28,656 cars to Europe, putting sales just ahead
of the pace last year, when it exported 53,331 cars to Europe.
(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
MUNICH - Telecommunications expert Peter Pribilla joins the
board of Siemens while Walter Kunerth steps down. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - Christoph Selig is named sales director of Epson's
German unit in Hanover. He was previously with Toshiba Europe.
(Kress)
